member.summary: Represents the encodation used to generate the DataMatrix barcode.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.Ascii
member.summary: Represents the ASCII encodation. Allowed characters include double digit numerics and all values from the ASCII table.
member.remarks: The double digit numerics use 4 bits. The ASCII values in the 0-127 range use 8 bits. The ASCII values in 128-255 range use 16 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.C40
member.summary: Represents the C40 encodation. Used primarily for upper-case alphanumerics.
member.remarks: The upper-case alphanumeric characters use 5.33 bits. The lower-case and special characters use 10.66 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.Text
member.summary: Represents the Text encodation. Used primarily for lower-case alphanumerics.
member.remarks: The lower-case alphanumeric characters use 5.33 bits. The upper-case and special characters use 10.66 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.X12
member.summary: Represents the X12 encodation. Uses the characters from ANSI X12 EDI data set.
member.remarks: Each character takes 5.33 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.Edifact
member.summary: Represents the EDIFACT encodation. Used to encode ASCII values in the 32-94 range.
member.remarks: Each character takes 6 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.Base256
member.summary: Represents the Base256 encodation. Used to encode characters in the whole ASCII range.
member.remarks: Each character takes 8 bits.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Barcode.Encodation.AsciiGS1
member.summary: Represents the ASCII GS1 encodation. Used to encode FNC1 characters in the ASCII range.

member.name: E:Telerik.Maui.Controls.RadCollectionView.LoadOnDemand
member.summary: Occurs when more items need to be loaded. When in Manual mode, the event is raised during the click of a button, presented as the last item in the CollectionView. When in Automatic mode, this event is raised while scrolling towards the end. You can use as an ItemsSource to automatically show loading indicator and load more items asynchronously, or you can manually fetch and add items to the source in this event. If you need to get more items async, you need to set the IsLoadOnDemandActive property to true before running the async call and set to false after adding the items to the ItemsSource. The event is not raised while the value of the IsLoadOnDemandActive property is true.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.RadCollectionView.IsLoadOnDemandEnabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the load-on-demand feature is enabled. This is the ability to load more items, either by pressing a button (Manual) or by scrolling towards the end (Automatic). You can get notifications when more items need to be loaded from the event, the or by using as ItemsSource.

member.summary: Gets a collection of validation rules associated with the current . member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.Controls.RadDataForm
member.summary: The is a customizable component which allows you to easily create an input form for manual data entry of business object data. The individual editors may either be inferred automatically from the metadata of the underlying business object data model or specified manually in XAML or code. The control supports different validation and commit modes, which makes it possible to validate or commit property values one by one or commit the entire data form at once. The control supports a rich set of pre-defined editors out of the box.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.DataGrid.DataGridColumn.DistinctValues
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom list of distinct values that are used when showing the . The provided list will be filtered by the built-in mechanism for choosing the values that will get displayed. The built-in mechanism works similar to Excel - the distinct values are filtered in a way to show as many values as possible except the ones that will lead to no results (an empty DataGrid). Technically this is done by using all items filtered with all filters in the DataGrid except the one associated with this column. To bypass the built-in logic you can use the event where you can provide a list of distinct values that will not be filtered or ordered.

member.name: M:Telerik.Maui.Controls.DataGrid.DataGridColumn.EfficientIntersect(System.Collections.IEnumerable,System.Collections.IEnumerable)
member.summary: A method that anticipates the lightCollection to be just a list (as it was provided by client dev) and for the heavyCollection to be a complex and potentially slow filtered enumerable (as is part of DG engine). That is why in this method we iterate the lightCollection first and while iterating the heavyCollection we stop right after we have found all items present in the lightCollection. This sort of optimization does not seem to happen with the System Linq Intersect. Also, the items yield in the same order as in the lightCollection collection.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Gauges.GaugeNeedleIndicator.Shape
member.summary: Gets or sets the path geometry that represents the shape of the needle. At run-time this geometry is scaled so that its width fits the diameter of the radial gauge (Position and Offset are also taken into account). In order for the needle to be positioned properly the positions of the provided geometry must be normalized between 0 and 1. The center of the needle is considered to be in the center of the normalized rectangle, i.e. (0.5, 0.5). The orientation of the needle is considered to be at 0 degrees from its center, i.e. the tip of the needle is at (1.0, 0.5).

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Gauges.GaugeRangeBarIndicator.GradientStops
member.summary: Gets the collection of gradient stops in accordance to which the bar is painted. The Offset property of the gradient stop is treated in respect to the IsOffsetRelative property value of the indicator.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Gauges.GaugeRangeBarIndicator.IsOffsetRelative
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Offset property of the gradient stops should be treated as a relative value between 0 and 1 or an absolute value in respect to the axis range.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Gauges.GaugeShapeIndicator.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the absolute size of the indicator.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Gauges.GaugeShapeIndicator.Shape
member.summary: Gets or sets the path geometry that represents the shape of the indicator. At run-time this geometry is positioned in accordance to the Position and Offset properties and is scaled in accordance to the Size property. In order for the shape to be positioned and scaled properly the positions of the provided geometry must be normalized between 0 and 1. The pivotal point of the shape is considered to be its center, i.e. (0.5, 0.5). The orientation of the indicator is considered to be from (1.0, 0.5) to its center.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Bottom
member.summary: A position of the Popup control where the control aligns its upper edge with the lower edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its left edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its lower edge aligns with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the upper screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control then repositions itself so that its upper edge aligns with the lower edge of the PlacementTarget and constraint its height.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Right
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns its left edge with the right edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its upper edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the right screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the left screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the right edge of the PlacementTarget and constrain its width.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Left
member.summary: A Popup control that aligns its right edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its upper edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget. If the left screen-edge obscures the Popup, the Popup repositions itself so that its left edge aligns with the right edge of the PlacementTarget. If the right screen-edge obscures the Popup, the right edge of the control aligns with the left edge of the PlacementTarget and constrain its width.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Top
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns its lower edge with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget and aligns its left edge with the left edge of the PlacementTarget. If the upper screen-edge obscures the Popup, the control repositions itself so that its upper edge aligns with the lower edge of the PlacementTarget. If the lower screen-edge obscures the Popup, the lower edge of the control aligns with the upper edge of the PlacementTarget and constrain its height.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Center
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns at the middle of the PlacementTarget.

member.name: F:Telerik.Maui.Controls.PlacementMode.Relative
member.summary: A position of the Popup control that aligns the top left corner of the popup with the top left corner of the placement target with the horizontal and vertical offset considered in the calculations.

member.summary: Get or sets a value indicating whether the header area is overlaid on top of the content area. When the overlay mode is enabled, the header area is centered and partially overlaps with one of the borders of the content area, based on the value of the property. The padding of the content area is adjusted accordingly, to avoid overlapping with the header area. When the overlay mode is disabled, the header area is placed adjacent to the content area without any overlapping, based on the value of the property.

member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.Controls.RadRangeSlider
member.summary: Represents a slider control that displays a start-end range in a given min-max range. The end user can change the values of the range by dragging the start thumb, end thumb, and range track. This control can display ticks and labels for clarity of what the underlying min-max range is, and can display tooltips for clarity of what the value corresponding to the dragged element is.

member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Scheduler.RecurrenceDays

summary.para: Specifies the days of the week. Members might be combined using bitwise operations to specify multiple days.

member.remarks: The constants in the enumeration might be combined with bitwise operations to represent any combination of days. It is designed to be used in conjunction with the class to filter the days of the week for which the recurrence pattern applies.

example.para: Consider the following example that demonstrates the basic usage pattern of RecurrenceDays. The most common operators used for manipulating bit fields are:

list.item: Bitwise OR: Turns a flag on.
Bitwise AND: Checks if a flag is turned on.
Bitwise NOT: Turns a flag off.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.MultidayViewDefinitionBase.MinTimeRulerExtent
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum size of the time ruler in pixels.
member.remarks: This property determines the minimum size of the time ruler in pixels. MinTimeRulerExtent of 1400 pixels means that the time ruler will be rendered with at least 1400 pixels no matter how much time it represents. If there is more than 1400 pixels available, it will be stretched as much as the value of the MaxTimeRulerExtent property allows to.
member.returns: The minimum size of the time ruler in pixels.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.MultidayViewDefinitionBase.MaxTimeRulerExtent
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum size of the time ruler in pixels.
member.remarks: This property determines the maximum size of the time ruler in pixels. MaxTimeRulerExtent of 1400 pixels means that the time ruler will be rendered with no more than 1400 pixels no matter how much time it represents. If there is less than 1400 pixels available, it will be squeezed as much as the value of the MinTimeRulerExtent property allows to.
member.returns: The maximum size of the time ruler in pixels.

member.summary: A markup extension that is used to color-blend.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Theming.ColorFilterExtension.Color
member.summary: The base color.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Theming.ColorFilterExtension.TintColor
member.summary:
Alpha blends the original Color with the TintColor one. The Red, Green, and Blue are linearly interpolated between the Color and the TintColor based on the TintColor's Alpha, the Alpha of the result preserves the Alpha of the original Color.
Useful to tint gradient shades.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Theming.ColorFilterExtension.Lighten
member.summary:
Expected to be in range [-1, 1]. For [-1, 0] will darken the Color, where -1 will result in black, -0.5 will be a dark version and 0 will preserve the Color. For [0, 1] will lighten the Color, where 1 will result in white, 0.5 will be a light version and 0 will preserve the Color.
Does not affect the Color's Alpha.

member.name: P:Telerik.Maui.Controls.Theming.ColorFilterExtension.Alpha
member.summary: When set, will be used as Alpha in the newly generated color, and will override the base Color's Alpha.

member.summary: The is a flexible control for implementation of tool and button strips, needed in most desktop and mobile applications. The individual items of the control are described as a collection of s. The rich collection of s allows to customize every tool or button on the independently according to the specific needs of the application. The control supports horizontal and vertical orientation, overflow menu, panning and scrolling, multi-level navigation and multi-line layout.

member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.Controls.GroupToolbarItemView
member.summary: Visual representation of a group of toolbar items in the control. The group works as a container of its child toolbar items keeping them in one place. For instance, when the group does not fit in the main strip area of the toolbar, all child toolbar items are moved to the overflow area together. Another use is to create two or more independent sets of radio buttons in the toolbar. Normally, only one radio button can be selected at a time. To create independent sets of radio buttons, they can be placed in separate groups.

member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.Controls.RadTreeDataGrid
member.summary: A component that presents hierarchical data with rows and columns. The control is given an ItemsSource and each item in that source is presented by a row. If an item has children, then each child is also presented by a row, recursively. Items that have children can be expanded and collapsed. This component can have columns, where each cell in the column contains the corresponding value for an item (for the row). This component inherits so almost all of its features will work here as well - like editing, cell templates, frozen columns, search, etc.

member.name: T:Telerik.Maui.ConstructHelper
member.summary: Why does this class exist? This class helps solve a peculiarity in the Maui framework - when there is an implicit style declared in App.xaml resources when an instance of the style's target type is created - property changed notifications are raised before the constructor is called (so before the object is intialized). Because of this, almost none of the private/internal fields have been initialized, and a null reference exception is thrown in the property changed handler when trying to acces some field. To work-around this, we use this class. Important - need to initialize this object via field initialization (before the ctor of the user-class). Important - need to call the method in the ctor user-class in the last row of the ctor. Important - each class needs his own private , instances should not be reused in inheritor classes.
